core_obligations: Take two representatives (V, g) and (V', g') of the rational map and record that they agree on a dense open W of V intersect V' (proof lines 9821-9822).
Show that the equalizer E of the two restrictions is a closed subspace of V intersect V' as the base change of the diagonal of Y (proof lines 9823-9826).
Use density of W in V intersect V' and reducedness to conclude that E = V intersect V' scheme theoretically, i.e. the two representatives agree on the whole intersection (proof lines 9827-9830).
Glue the representatives along the fppf surjection from the disjoint union of the V onto U to obtain the morphism f representing phi (proof lines 9831-9834).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: for a rational map phi from a reduced algebraic space X to a separated algebraic space Y over S, there is a unique morphism f : U -> Y on the domain of definition U representing phi (source lines 9811-9818). The proof compares two representatives (V, g) and (V', g'), which agree on a dense open W contained in V intersect V'; the equalizer E of the two restrictions is a closed subspace because it is the base change of the diagonal of Y, and since W is contained in E while W is dense, |E| equals |V intersect V'|; reducedness then upgrades this to E = V intersect V' scheme theoretically, so the representatives glue along the fppf surjection from the disjoint union of the V to U.
